texts.preamble: Munna Lal vs State Of U.P. on 29 March, 2024 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:54271 Court No. - 74 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 3162 of 2008 Revisionist :- Munna Lal Opposite Party :- State of U.P. Counsel for Revisionist :- Dheeraj Singh Bohra,Krishna Mohan Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1. List revised.
texts.facts: 5. The case of the prosecution as initiated on the basis of a complaint dated 24.01.2002 filed by the Food Inspector J.P. Tripathi for offences under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is that on 27.12.2002 at about 10:00 am while being on regular inspection he reached Bareilly Mod Crossing where he found the accused Munna Lal present in a shop which had Peda, Barfi, Samosa, Tea etc. for human consumption to be sold. The said food articles were kept in open and were thus found exposed to dust and flies were sitting on it. He asked for a license of the shop which could not be shown by the accused. The material was considered by him to be unfit for human consumption. He gave his introduction to the people present there and asked them to be witness of the raid to which the people refused. He then filed a complaint dated 24.01.2002 for offences punishable under Section 7(iii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 49, 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 against the revisionist. 6. The trial court framed charges against the revisionist vide order dated 06.04.2004 for offence under Section 7/16 of the Food Adulteration Act. 7. In the trial, the complainant J.P. Tripathi was examined as PW-1. The accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. took up the case that he has a PCO beside the said shop and filed its demand letter, telephone bill and filed a license issued under the Food Adulteration Act in the name of Shyam Babu for the said shop which was raided. Shyam Babu was produced as DW-1. The present revision has thus been filed before this Court.
texts.arguments: 9. Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that the revisionist has been falsely implicated in the present case. It is submitted that no sample of any food material was taken by the complainant/Food Inspector to substantiate the claim of the material being unfit for human consumption and adulterated. It is submitted that there is no public witness of the incident which is Munna Lal vs State Of U.P. on 29 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128540476/ 2 the admitted case of the prosecution case. It is further argued that in so far as the case of the revisionist that he is not the owner of the shop in question but is the owner of a PCO beside the said shop and further that license of the said shop is in the name of Shyam Babu for selling food items has not been found to be false by the trial court. It is submitted that in so far as the license for selling food items is concerned, the same was not disputed to be not of the said shop and in the name of Shyam Babu the brother of the revisionist and a disputed document. It is argued that no sample of the material alleged to be adulterated and found to be infested with dust on which flies were said to be sitting, was collected as sample by the Food Analyst/Complainant/PW-1 for sending it to analyst for reaching to a conclusion of the same to be unfit for human consumption. It is submitted that the appellate court has without going into merits of the matter and without recording the arguments of the appeal and also without appreciating the evidence of a sole prosecution witness, the defence of the revisionist accused as stated under Section 313 Cr.P.C., the defence documents and defence witness Shyam Babu DW-1 dismissed the appeal in a very cryptic manner by just recording a finding that there is no irregularity or illegality in the judgment of the trial court and as such the appeal is rejected. It is argued that there is no credible evidence to connect the revisionist in the present case. It is argued that the revision be thus allowed. 10. Learned counsel for the Sate per contra opposed the revision vehemently and submitted that the trial court has given cogent and justifiable findings while convicting the revisionist after holding him guilty in the matter.
